explanation:
Code facts: POST /preference (app.py:0085-0087) forwards purpose/value to store.preference, which accepts only purposes insights/promotions/objection and values on/off and inserts a row into choices with value=int(value=="on"), version=VERSION and a UTC timestamp (store.py:0092-0095; schema store.py:0042; VERSION store.py:0011). enabled() selects the latest choices row WHERE owner=? AND purpose=? and returns False when no row matches (store.py:0088-0090). Insights processing is gated twice: the report action requires enabled(who,"insights") before queueing (store.py:0167-0168), and the drain "report" branch executes only when enabled(c["owner"],"insights") (store.py:0137-0139). Campaign eligibility reads only enabled(...,"promotions") and not enabled(...,"objection") (store.py:0100-0103), and the promotion drain branch uses eligible_campaign (store.py:0140-0141). submit() validates only application fields and inserts the case with no reference to choices or enabled (store.py:0065-0083); the dashboard application form carries no consent checkbox (views.py:0031-0032), while per-purpose switch forms submit explicit on/off values (views.py:0033-0036). An "off" insights choice appends a new row and cancels queued report jobs (store.py:0096-0098).

Requirement: The predicate requires that optional repayment-insights processing be gated on a purpose-specific, affirmative, versioned consent record for purpose "insights"; that a "promotions" choice cannot satisfy that gate; and that the core application remain usable with insights off. The scenario supplies the trigger (adult EU controller, insights initially off, marketing permission not authorizing insights) and no exception applies, since this is a consent-gating predicate rather than a derogation.

Justification: The exact-purpose lookup in enabled() means a promotions row cannot satisfy an insights query, and the absence of any row yields False, matching the "initially off" scenario and the affirmative-opt-in requirement; each choice is persisted with a version and timestamp, satisfying the versioned-record element. Both the queue-time and drain-time insights gates query purpose "insights", and the promotions path never consults "insights", so a promotions choice cannot authorize insights. submit() and the dashboard form have no consent dependency, so the core application remains available with insights off. No in-scope counterexample was found in the supplied source; the verdict rests on static source reading only, with no execution performed.

evidence.supports: enabled() reads the latest choices row for the exact (owner,purpose); no row => False, so insights default off and a promotions row cannot satisfy an insights query.

evidence.quote:
def preference(db, who, purpose, value):
    require(who in CUSTOMERS and purpose in ("insights","promotions","objection") and value in ("on","off"),"Invalid preference.")
    db.execute("INSERT INTO choices(owner,purpose,value,version,at) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
               (who,purpose,int(value=="on"),VERSION,datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()))
    if (purpose,value)==("insights","off") or (purpose,value) in (("promotions","off"),("objection","on")):
        kind = "report" if purpose=="insights" else "promotion"
        db.execute("UPDATE jobs SET state='cancelled' WHERE kind=? AND state='queued' AND cid IN (SELECT id FROM cases WHERE owner=?)",(kind,who))
evidence.supports: preference() restricts purposes to insights/promotions/objection and values to on/off, persists int(value=='on') with VERSION and timestamp, and cancels queued report jobs on insights off.

evidence.quote: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS choices(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, purpose TEXT, value INTEGER, version TEXT, at TEXT);
evidence.supports: choices schema stores owner, purpose, value, version, at — the versioned consent record.
VERSION constant written into each choice row.
drain 'report' branch executes insights processing only when enabled(owner,'insights').
report action requires enabled(who,'insights') before queueing; promotion action uses eligible_campaign (promotions purpose only).
eligible_campaign reads only 'promotions' and 'objection' purposes, never 'insights'.

def submit(db, who, data):
    require(who in CUSTOMERS,"Borrower account required.",403)
    require(set(data) <= {"email","amount","term","income","auto"},"Unexpected application field.")
    try:
        amount, term = int(data.get("amount","")), int(data.get("term",""))
    except ValueError:
        raise Problem("Enter a valid amount and term.")
    require(100 <= amount <= 100000 and term in (6,12,24,36),"Amount or term outside available range.")
    income = data.get("income","")
    require(income in LIMITS and data.get("auto","") in ("","yes"),"Invalid application choice.")
    route = "automatic" if data.get("auto")=="yes" else "manual"
    officer = dict(zip(CUSTOMERS,OFFICERS))[who]
    cid = db.execute("INSERT INTO cases(owner,officer,email,amount,term,income,route,stage) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                     (who,officer,email(data.get("email","")),amount,term,income,route,"pending")).lastrowid
    db.execute("INSERT INTO summaries VALUES(?,?)",(cid,f"EUR {amount:,} · {term} months"))
    event(db,cid,"application",f"{route} route selected under notice {VERSION}")
    if route=="automatic":
        queue(db,cid,"score")
    return cid
evidence.supports: submit() validates only application fields and inserts the case; no consent/choices dependency, so core application remains available with insights off.
